approach: Add one pure reading check, `check_behavior_test_design`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, wired as one `step!` line directly after `check_code_survey`. It reads only the reading (the `Code survey:` assumptions, criteria and deliverables). It parses the survey into labelled clauses (`Entry point:`, `Gate order:`, `Stop gate:`, `Reuses:`, `Output:`, `Direct check:`) and judges each clause alone. (a) The `Gate order:` clause lists at least two identifiers, and the `Stop gate:` clause names one of them. (b) The `Reuses:` clause names an identifier or says "no existing function"; partial reuse is accepted. (c) The `Output:` clause says "no new output", or names record evidence through the existing `names_record_evidence` or a schema tag `athena.<kind>/<n>`. A typed record needs a round-trip identifier that a behavior criterion also names, plus a listed crates/ deliverable. (d) Each behavior criterion is covered by a `Direct check:` clause that states a measurement, and no skip switch or internal-helper read is the means of measurement. Negators and refusal words cancel a skip-switch or helper phrase anywhere earlier in the same clause or sentence, so the request's own wording and the plan's template are accepted. The error names each missing letter and each contradiction and gives a one-line template. No repository is read, because the reading gate runs without one (replay.rs:50-55), so "contradicts the code" is limited to contradicting a rule this check enforces or the reading itself; the doc comment says so. The existing short `Code survey:` fixtures are replaced by one complete survey. The 20% share is declared by the reading's criterion 4. This plan does not weaken the check to meet it. The honest share is probably higher (see open question).

decisions.choice: Judge the survey by labelled clauses, not by whole-text phrase search. Each part is read inside its own clause. A clause runs from its label (case-insensitive, at the start of the text or after whitespace or a full stop) to the next label. A repeated label, or a label in a second `Code survey:` assumption, adds to the same clause. Position finding uses ASCII lowercase on whitespace-normalised original text, so identifier case (`AnyRecord`) is kept for `names_record_evidence`.
decisions.reason: This answers findings 3 and 6. A phrase such as 'directly' or 'calls' in a description of the code (`refusing_check` calls each step directly) can no longer stand for a measurement. The stop gate is looked up only against the `Gate order:` clause, not any earlier text. The reading is a plain `Vec<String>` of assumptions (surveys.rs:117-124), so labels are the only structure available without changing the Reading type.

rejected.option: Keep whole-survey phrase search with a stop-gate identifier 'earlier in the text'
rejected.why: A name in the list of paths read would pass, and 'directly' plus 'calls' anywhere would satisfy (d) for every criterion.

rejected.option: Add typed fields to the Reading for the four parts
rejected.why: This changes the reading schema in athena-data and the reader prompt, which is out of scope and has 2 tokens of headroom.

decisions.choice: (a) The `Entry point:` clause must hold an identifier. The `Gate order:` clause must hold at least two distinct identifiers. The `Stop gate:` clause must hold an identifier that is equal to one of the gate-order identifiers. An identifier is a whitespace token (backticks and trailing punctuation trimmed) that has `_` or `::`, or that ended in `()`. A stop gate written only in prose has no identifier and is refused as missing (a). A stop gate named in the survey but absent from the gate order is refused as a contradiction.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 6. The plan states the prose case outright and adds a fixture for it. The term ladder's 'resolution and probing steps' must be written as identifiers to count.

rejected.why: The point of (a) is that the test stops at a named gate; prose names none that the check can compare with the order.

decisions.choice: (b) Accept a `Reuses:` clause that holds an identifier, or the phrase 'no existing function', or both. Refuse only an absent or empty clause, or one with neither. Drop the 'no existing function beside a reuse' contradiction.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Partial reuse ('reuses `names_record_evidence`; no existing function checks gate order, so one is added') is the shape of this job's own accepted reading, and the plan's template holds both phrases.

rejected.why: A false positive on the normal case, and it would refuse the template the error text gives.

decisions.choice: (c) The `Output:` clause is accepted when it says 'no new output' or 'no new record' with no record or data deliverable, or when `names_record_evidence` is true for it, or when it holds a schema tag found by a new helper `names_schema_tag` (a token that starts `athena.` and has `/` then digits). The tag helper handles only the tag form. `names_record_evidence` already matches `AnyRecord::<Variant>` and `check_record_file` (surveys.rs:164-175), so there is no second matcher for those. A round-trip identifier is the one predicate shared with `names_record_evidence`. It is pulled out of that function as `is_round_trip_token` with no behaviour change. A typed record that names only a round-trip identifier needs a behavior criterion that names the same kind of identifier, plus at least one listed crates/ deliverable. A record or data deliverable (`is_record_or_data_deliverable`) beside 'no new output' is a contradiction.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 7: no near-duplicate matcher. Real accepted kinds are the `AnyRecord` variants and their tags (records.rs:1125-1147). The check cannot confirm a named kind exists without a repository, so it checks the form. That limit goes in the doc comment.

rejected.why: Near-duplicate of `names_record_evidence`; the request forbids it.

rejected.option: A public list of accepted kinds added to athena-data and checked here
rejected.why: Edits records.rs, which would itself trigger the record-evidence rule, and is not a listed deliverable.

decisions.choice: (d) The survey needs `Direct check:` clauses. Each must state a measurement: one of `count`, `counts`, `counting`, `counted`, `asserts`, `asserting`, `compares`, `observes`. Each behavior criterion number must be covered by a clause that cites it (`criterion 2`, `criteria 2 and 3`, `criteria 2-3`). A clause that cites no number covers all behavior criteria only when the reading has exactly one. Uncovered criterion numbers are listed in the error.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. The request says a direct check for each claimed property. One statement can no longer cover many criteria, and the fixture 'directly and calls only in code description' is refused. Limit stated in the doc: a clause can name a measurement that is untrue, and the plan critic and verifier judge that.

rejected.option: One global pair of words ('directly' plus 'calls')
rejected.why: Satisfied by prose about the code, and one statement covers any number of criteria.

decisions.choice: Skip-switch and internal-helper contradictions are scoped to the means of measurement. The phrases are `skip switch`, `skip flag`, `test-only switch`, `--skip`, `internal helper`, `private helper`. In a `Direct check:` clause an occurrence counts unless a cancel word (`no`, `not`, `never`, `without`, `nor`, `instead of`, `refuse`, `refuses`, `refused`, `reject`, `rejects`) stands anywhere earlier in the same clause. In a behavior criterion it counts only when a means word (`through`, `via`, `by`, `using`, `with`, `read`, `reads`, `reading`, `inspects`) is within 4 words before it, in the same sentence, with no cancel word earlier in that sentence. Fixtures use the request's exact wording ('not reads of an internal helper and not a skip switch added just for the test'), this job's criterion 3 text, and the plan's own template verbatim; all three must be accepted.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The 3-word window put `not` four words from 'internal helper' in the request's wording. A negator anywhere earlier in the clause or sentence cancels, as the existing `requires_existing_code_section` does through a later anchor (surveys.rs:1359-1393). A criterion that only describes the rule is not a contradiction.

rejected.option: A fixed 3-word negation lookback over the whole survey and every criterion
rejected.why: Refuses the request's wording, the template and this job's own criterion 3.

rejected.option: Refuse on any mention, as `check_history_fixture` does
rejected.why: Refuses the sentence the reader is asked to write.

decisions.choice: A new function and a new `step!` line, not a growth of `check_code_survey`. Refusals are counted under their own rule name.
decisions.reason: `refusing_check` says each check is one `step!` line (checks.rs:515-516), and the corpus test pins a refusing case per step. The existing survey tests assert that check's text (reading.rs ~7071-7167). The new name gets its own row in the per-rule counts, which key on the string `refusing_check` returns, so status.rs needs no edit.

rejected.why: Its error text and counts would change, and refusals would be counted under the old rule name.

decisions.choice: Do not weaken the check to meet the replay limit. The declared share stays 'expected 20% of newly refused readings' as the accepted reading and criterion 4 fix it. The real share is not measured. Part of the open question asks the user to decide.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. `replay_cases` replays the newest 50 accepted readings (replay.rs:9, 140-156). Accepted code readings with a behavior criterion mostly have a short survey and no labelled parts, so they would be newly refused. Spelling widening cannot make a reading that never mentions a gate order pass. The 'widen the spellings' mitigation is removed. A declared share above 25 is applied only with a reason sentence ('because' plus 'refuse' or 'past readings', replay.rs:170-186, 202-205), which needs a revised reading, and not a code change.

rejected.option: Loosen markers until the replay passes
rejected.why: It would defeat the purpose and hide the fact the check refuses most past code readings.

decisions.choice: The fixture replay test builds each case so that every later check accepts it. For each case the new step refuses, the test asserts that the same reading with the complete survey is accepted by `check_reading_text`. The base checker is `check_reading_text` on the reading with its survey swapped for the complete one.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. The step cannot be skipped inside `refusing_check`. Proving the later checks accept the reading shows the refusal is new and the base build would accept it, so the newly-refused count is true.

rejected.option: A base closure that turns a `check_behavior_test_design` refusal into Accept
rejected.why: It skips the later steps, which may refuse the reading in the real base build.

decisions.choice: status.rs and replay.rs are left unchanged, with the reason in the producer report. briefs/reader.rs and briefs.rs change only if the brief test still passes without raising `READING_RULES_BASELINE_BYTES`.
decisions.reason: status.rs:3908 has `RULE_B` as a test string only and the stats key on whatever name is returned. replay.rs already holds the declared share plus 5 points (replay.rs:159-165, 289-308). The reader brief section is at its byte baseline, so raising the baseline would weaken the guard.

rejected.option: Edit both files to match the deliverables list
rejected.why: Empty churn; an unchanged planned file is reported with a reason.

rejected.option: Raise the baseline or add a 13th rule line
rejected.why: It weakens the brief's size guard and breaks the 12-line pin.

steps: Step 1, surveys.rs helpers: extract `is_round_trip_token(token: &str) -> bool` from `names_record_evidence` and call it there (no behaviour change). Add `names_schema_tag(text)` (token starts `athena.`, has `/` then digits). Add `survey_clauses(surveys: &[&str])`: join the `Code survey:` assumptions after whitespace normalisation, find the labels `entry point:`, `gate order:`, `stop gate:`, `reuses:`, `output:`, `direct check:` on an ASCII-lowercase copy (same byte offsets) at the start of the text or after whitespace or a full stop, and return each label's clause text from the original string up to the next label; a repeated label appends. Add `identifiers(clause)`: whitespace tokens with backticks and trailing punctuation trimmed, kept when they contain `_` or `::` or ended in `()`. Add a `cancelled_before(text, at)` helper over the cancel words and a `means_phrase` finder for the skip-switch and internal-helper phrases.

Step 2, surveys.rs check: add `pub fn check_behavior_test_design(reading) -> Result<()>`. Return Ok unless `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion(reading)`. Take `code_surveys(reading)` and build the clauses. Collect problems per letter. (a) `Entry point:` has an identifier; `Gate order:` has at least two distinct identifiers; `Stop gate:` has an identifier, and that identifier equals one in the gate order (else 'stop gate not in the stated gate order'; with no identifier, 'stop gate missing'). (b) `Reuses:` has an identifier or `has_phrase(.., "no existing function")`. (c) `Output:` passes when it has `no new output` or `no new record` and no `is_record_or_data_deliverable` deliverable exists (else contradiction), or `names_record_evidence(clause)` or `names_schema_tag(clause)` holds; a clause with only a round-trip identifier also needs a behavior criterion with a round-trip token and a listed crates/ deliverable. (d) Each `Direct check:` clause has a measurement verb; every behavior criterion number is cited by a clause (`criterion N`, `criteria N and M`, `criteria N-M`), or the reading has exactly one behavior criterion and a clause cites none. Contradictions (d): an uncancelled skip-switch or internal-helper phrase in a `Direct check:` clause, or as the means in a behavior criterion (a means word within 4 words before, none cancelling earlier in the sentence). Collect every problem into one `bail!` that starts 'the reading was refused because', names each of (a)-(d) and each contradiction, and gives the template: `Code survey: <paths>. Entry point: `f`. Gate order: `g1`, `g2`, `g3`. Stop gate: `g2`. Reuses: `h`; no existing function does X. Output: `AnyRecord::<Kind>` or no new output. Direct check: criterion 2 counts planner, producer or model calls on the fake, not a skip switch or a read of an internal helper.` Write the full doc comment (cause, gate, limits, declared share).

Step 3, checks.rs: add `step!(check_behavior_test_design(reading));` directly after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));` and extend the `check_reading_acceptance` doc comment (475-491) with the link, in order. Import the function the way `check_code_survey` is imported.

Step 4, reading.rs tests (fixtures): make `SURVEY` (~7037) the complete labelled survey (crates path; entry point `refusing_check`; gate order `check_criteria_evidence`, `check_code_survey`, `check_history_fixture`; stop gate `check_code_survey`; reuses `names_record_evidence` plus 'no existing function checks gate order'; output no new output; direct check citing criterion 1 that counts calls). It holds no record evidence, so the tests that expect `crates/foo/records/one.rs` to be refused (~7191-7199) still hold. Change the record-evidence tests (~7148-7157) to `&[SURVEY, evidence]` and use an Output clause that does not say 'no new output' where a record deliverable is listed. Update `history_fixture_has_one_step_line` (~8206-8230) so `steps[survey+1]` is the new step and `steps[survey+2]` the history line. Add `design_check_has_one_step_line_after_the_survey_step` and a doc test that `check_reading_acceptance`'s doc links the check. Run the whole reading test module and fix each fixture that still expects the old acceptance.

Step 5, reading.rs tests (omissions): add `design_check_refuses_each_omitted_part` (four readings each missing one of (a)-(d); assert `refusing_check` name and that the error names only that letter), `design_check_refuses_a_prose_stop_gate`, `design_check_refuses_direct_check_words_only_in_code_description`, `design_check_refuses_an_uncovered_behavior_criterion` (two behavior criteria, one cited), and `design_check_accepts_a_complete_reading` with the accepted variants: parts spread over two `Code survey:` assumptions, labels in other case with extra spaces, partial reuse, identifiers as `f()` and `a::b`.

Step 6, reading.rs tests (contradictions): add `design_check_contradiction_refuses_*` for a stop gate absent from the order, a record or data deliverable beside 'no new output', a typed record with no round-trip identifier or tag, a round-trip identifier no criterion names, a `Direct check:` through a skip switch, and a criterion that checks by reading an internal helper. Add accepted twins: the negated form, the request's exact wording, the plan template verbatim and this job's criterion 3 text. Add `design_check_does_not_apply_outside_its_gate` (docs class, decline, question, content-only criteria).

Step 7, reading.rs tests (replay and docs): add `design_check_replay_share_is_within_the_declared_range` with 10 cases built so every later check accepts them. For each newly refused case, assert the same reading with the complete survey is accepted by `check_reading_text`. The base is `check_reading_text` on the swapped reading and the candidate is `check_reading_text` on the reading as it is. Declare 20 with a criterion 'expected 20% of newly refused readings'; assert not held, at least 1 newly refused, at most 25%. Add a second run whose candidate refuses every code reading and assert held. Add a test like `code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended` (~7233) for the new doc comment and changelog sentences.

Step 8, refusal_corpus.rs: add `COMPLETE_SURVEY` and use it at lines 352, 2035 and 2043. Add the cases listed in demonstrations 2 and 3 (refusing: `design-missing-gate-order-and-stop-gate`, `design-missing-reused-function`, `design-missing-record-kind-or-roundtrip`, `design-missing-direct-check`, `design-stop-gate-in-prose`, `design-direct-check-words-only-in-code-description`, `design-stop-gate-not-in-order`, `design-new-typed-record-without-roundtrip-deliverable`, `design-record-deliverable-beside-no-new-output`, `design-criterion-uses-skip-switch`, `design-criterion-reads-internal-helper`; accepting: `design-complete-reading-accepted`, `design-partial-reuse-accepted`, `design-split-across-surveys-accepted`, `design-negated-skip-switch-accepted`, `design-request-wording-accepted`, `design-template-verbatim-accepted`, `design-docs-class-not-checked`). Add 11 `INPUT_FORMS` tags: `design-part-missing`, `design-stop-gate-in-prose`, `design-stop-gate-not-in-order`, `design-partial-reuse`, `design-typed-record`, `design-skip-switch-or-helper`, `design-negated-phrase`, `design-direct-check-per-criterion`, `design-complete`, `design-split-across-surveys`, `design-outside-gate`; change the array length 63 to 74. The existing cases `code-reading-without-a-survey` (2014, still refused earlier by `check_code_survey`), `code-reading-with-a-survey` (2025, now with the complete survey, Accept), and the history cases at 2042+ (`landing-rule-on-job-commits-only-job-1rve`, `commit-shape-rule-without-a-fixture-job-e65v` and later ones, which use the complete survey so they still reach `check_history_fixture`) cover the pre-existing forms.

Step 9, briefs/reader.rs and briefs.rs: reword the `Code survey` line (~291) in place to name the labels and `check_behavior_test_design`, within 220 bytes, 12 rules, and the section at or below `READING_RULES_BASELINE_BYTES`; trim words elsewhere in the section if needed. Add the check name to the list at briefs.rs ~3639-3650. If the size test cannot pass without raising the baseline, revert this step and leave both files unchanged.

Step 10, CHANGELOG.md and checks: add the `[Unreleased]` `### Added` entry. Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`, `cargo test -p athena-context`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. In the report, say why status.rs and replay.rs are unchanged.

risks.risk: The real newly refused share exceeds the declared 20% plus 5 points, so the host replay holds the job. Records are not in the snapshot, so no step can measure it.
risks.mitigation: The check is not loosened to fit the number. The fixture test proves the arithmetic only. The producer loop runs the same replay and reports the limit (`replay_limit_percent`). The open question asks the user to revise the declared share with a reason or accept a hold. The share is labelled an estimate until the host replay records it.

risks.risk: The check is lexical and cannot see the repository. It cannot tell that a named function or record kind does not exist, or that a stated measurement is untrue.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment says so, like `check_history_fixture` and `check_records_measure`. `check_reading_references` still compares paths when files are known. The planner's dependents list, the plan critic and the verifier remain the guard for function-level facts.

risks.risk: Labelled clauses make the check strict about format: a reader that writes the right content without the labels is refused.
risks.mitigation: The error names each missing part and gives a one-line template with the labels. Labels match in any case, and parts may be spread over several `Code survey:` assumptions. The reader brief line names the labels if it fits.

risks.risk: Fixture drift: tests that use the short survey and expect refusal by a later check are refused first by the new step and fail.
risks.mitigation: Steps 3 and 8 replace every short survey. The producer greps for `Code survey:` and `SURVEY` in reading.rs and refusal_corpus.rs and runs `cargo test -p athena-core` before finishing.

risks.risk: The reader brief section is at its byte baseline, so rewording the rule line can fail the size test.
risks.mitigation: Reword in place and trim other words. If it cannot pass, the brief edit is dropped, which criterion 6 allows. The refusal text still gives the template.

risks.risk: status.rs and replay.rs are listed deliverables but need no change, and an unchanged planned file is reported to the producer as left unchanged without a reason.
risks.mitigation: The producer report says why for each: stats key on the step name string, and replay already holds a declared share plus 5 points. Both reasons are in decisions.

demonstrations.fails_without: Without the function and the step line, the grep finds neither and the step-order test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Static grep plus the unit test over `refusing_check`'s source text, the same technique as `history_fixture_has_one_step_line` (reading.rs ~8206, exists). Step 4 adds the new test.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs and corpus cases in refusal_corpus.rs run the real gate on four otherwise complete code readings, each omitting one part, and on one complete reading. The tests are written by the plan's steps and not yet run.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core design_check && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: `design_check_refuses_each_omitted_part` builds four readings from `code_reading` and the complete survey. They lack respectively: the gate order and stop gate (a); the `Reuses:` clause (b); the `Output:` kind or the round-trip identifier (c); the `Direct check:` clause (d). Each asserts `refusing_check` returns `check_behavior_test_design` and that the error names only the omitted letter. Another fixture has 'directly' and 'calls' only in a description of the code outside a `Direct check:` clause, and is refused on (d). Another has a stop gate written in prose, refused on (a). Another has two behavior criteria and a `Direct check:` clause citing only one, refused on (d) with the uncovered number. `design_check_accepts_a_complete_reading` asserts `check_reading_acceptance` is Ok, as do parts spread over two `Code survey:` assumptions, labels in other case with extra spaces, and the partial-reuse form. Corpus ids: `design-missing-gate-order-and-stop-gate`, `design-missing-reused-function`, `design-missing-record-kind-or-roundtrip`, `design-missing-direct-check`, `design-stop-gate-in-prose`, `design-direct-check-words-only-in-code-description` (Refuse `check_behavior_test_design`); `design-complete-reading-accepted`, `design-partial-reuse-accepted`, `design-split-across-surveys-accepted` (Accept).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, `check_code_survey` accepts all four incomplete readings because it needs only a crates/ path (surveys.rs:203-216). The refuser assertions fail, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails if the step exists with no refusing case.
demonstrations.seam: Production entries `check_behavior_test_design`, `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:492-551, exist). Fixtures: `code_reading` and `SURVEY` (reading.rs ~7037-7060, exist; step 3 makes `SURVEY` the complete survey) and the corpus `base_reading`/`case` helpers (refusal_corpus.rs ~172, 241, exist). Plain `Reading` values are passed in; there is no double. The check is a pure function and no model is called.

demonstrations.method: Unit and corpus fixtures that each change one field of a complete reading to contradict a rule, plus negated and verbatim twins that must be accepted.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core design_check_contradiction && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: Refused with `check_behavior_test_design`: a stop gate not in the `Gate order:` clause; a record or data deliverable (`crates/athena-data/src/records.rs`, or a created `crates/.../records/x.json`) beside 'Output: no new output'; a typed record with no round-trip identifier and no schema tag; a typed record with a round-trip identifier no behavior criterion names; a `Direct check:` clause that measures 'through a skip switch'; a behavior criterion that says the property is checked 'by reading an internal helper'. Accepted (twins): 'counts planner calls on the fake, not a skip switch or a read of an internal helper'; the request's exact wording 'not reads of an internal helper and not a skip switch added just for the test'; the plan's template verbatim; this job's own criterion 3 text. Corpus ids: `design-stop-gate-not-in-order`, `design-new-typed-record-without-roundtrip-deliverable`, `design-record-deliverable-beside-no-new-output`, `design-criterion-uses-skip-switch`, `design-criterion-reads-internal-helper` (Refuse); `design-negated-skip-switch-accepted`, `design-request-wording-accepted`, `design-template-verbatim-accepted` (Accept).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the contradiction rules the part labels are all present and the readings pass, so the refusal assertions fail. The accepted twins fail on a version that refuses on any mention or uses a 3-word window.
demonstrations.seam: Same production entries and fixtures as criterion 2. Step 1 adds the clause parser, the cancel-word logic and `names_schema_tag`; the tests call the production function on a reading with one field changed.

demonstrations.method: Two parts. (1) A fixture replay through the production `replay` function, to prove the declared-share arithmetic and that the new rule is newly refusing. (2) Athena's own replay at verification on the real records. Part (1) does not measure the real share.
demonstrations.observes: (1) `design_check_replay_share_is_within_the_declared_range` builds 10 `ReplayCase` values: 2 code readings with the old short survey (newly refused), 4 with the complete survey, 4 docs readings. Every case passes all later checks. For each newly refused case it asserts that the reading with the complete survey is accepted by `check_reading_text`. The base checker is `check_reading_text` on that swapped reading; the candidate is `check_reading_text` on the reading as it is. It takes the declaration from `replay_declaration_of` on a reading whose criterion reads 'expected 20% of newly refused readings', and asserts `!run.held`, at least 1 newly refused, and `newly_refused * 100 <= total * replay_limit_percent(Some(20))`. A second run with a candidate that refuses every code reading asserts `run.held`. (2) At verification the host runs `replay_cases` over the newest 50 accepted readings (replay.rs:9, 140-156, run/mod.rs ~2246-2402) and records the Replay. State needed: the host's `records/` with accepted readings. This plan neither runs nor waits for it; the verifier reads the recorded Replay and its `held` flag. The real share is unmeasured, and is likely above 20%.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check newly refused more than 25% of the fixtures, `run.held` is true and the assertion fails. If it refused nothing, the 'at least 1' assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entries `replay`, `replay_declaration_of`, `replay_limit_percent` and `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54, 289-308, 365; exist). `ReplayCase` values and the checker closures are built in the test via the existing `replay_case` helper and `base_checker` pattern (reading.rs ~6466-6545, exist); step 7 adds the test. The closures only call `check_reading_text`; the logic under test is the production check.

open_questions: User: The accepted reading fixes 'expected 20% of newly refused readings' (limit 25% with the 5-point margin). Most accepted code readings in the newest 50 probably carry only a short `Code survey:` with none of the labelled parts, so the real newly refused share is probably well above 25%, and the host replay would then hold this job at verification. Code cannot show the real share, because records/ is not in the snapshot. Do you want the reading revised to declare a higher share with a reason sentence (a criterion with 'because' and 'refuse(d)' or 'past readings', which `replay_declaration` accepts above 25%), or accept that the job may be held?
